bug_semantics: OS command injection in the macOS screenshot auto-paste path of browser-tools-server/browser-connector.ts. An untrusted directory path from the unauthenticated WebSocket screenshot-data message (and/or HTTP /screenshot body or merged settings.screenshotPath) becomes targetPath, is joined into fullPath, then interpolated into AppleScript as set imagePath to "${fullPath}" and executed via child_process.exec(`osascript -e '${appleScript}'`). A single quote in the path breaks the shell single-quoted -e argument and yields arbitrary command execution on darwin when that branch runs. The 1.x connector also bound 0.0.0.0 with open CORS, so the sink was remotely reachable. At first write the darwin branch ran unconditionally after save; 03cb3ca later gated it on autoPaste===true without changing the interpolation.
flaw_origin: b829891e541a6e0ab080b3b77901ea43bde962ea ("Added auto-paste of screenshot into cursor for macos") is the first public write of the osascript exec sink. It added +161 lines inside BrowserConnector.captureScreenshot: after saving the PNG it always, on darwin, built appleScript with unsanitized fullPath and called exec. Parent bc4629db97d191251ad701fc6a063f284397a9ca already had captureScreenshot, customPath/outputPath, and the save, but no AppleScript/osascript/exec of that path. Repo-wide -S osascript has only this introducer and the 2.0 rewrite that deletes it. Not a move, squash, revert, or backport.

reasoning: The vulnerability is real CWE-77/78: unsanitized caller-controlled filesystem path is interpolated into a shell-invoked osascript -e string. Smallest first-write is b829891, which created that exec sink; the parent already saved screenshots to an attacker-influenced path but did not execute it. Later autoPaste toggle and 1.2.0 packaging are not the origin. 1d1b8eb is the closing fix (2.0 rewrite removes the connector and the AppleScript/exec path).
